body:
Follow-ups surfaced during the real-Oracle dogfood pass (`t_3e1b03bf`) on `e18c9b6`:

1. **Accepted deck has empty `color` (`reconstruct.py:560` / `reconstruct_builder.py:344`)**: `accept_draft` reads `draft.get('color', '')`, but `ReconstructBuilder.build()` never sets `color` on draft dicts even though commander colour identity is resolved during validation.
2. **UI build polling stops at 60s (`templates/reconstruct.html:1648`)**: `startPolling()` sets `maxAttempts = 60` (1s interval), showing `Draft generation is taking longer than expected` after 60s while real Oracle builds take ~220–400s (`ORACLE_TIMEOUT_S=600`).
3. **Single Oracle 600s timeout fails build without retry**: `ReconstructBuilder.build()` retries validation errors up to `max_retries`, but a single `OracleUnavailable` client timeout aborts immediately.
title: Reconstruct dogfood follow-ups: draft color identity, UI 60s poll timeout, Oracle timeout retry

Found in design review of PR #145, head e495450. Severity: Medium (on phones the Save/Discard bar is hidden while a list is open).

**Repro:** 375x812 viewport, touch emulation. Scroll to Kindred, focus the input, type `e`.
**Expected:** The list is fully visible above the sticky save bar and scrollable.
**Actual:** The listbox is `position:absolute` under the field and never scrolls into view. The Kindred list spans y 764 to 817 (viewport 812), so it is clipped and covers the save bar. With a simulated keyboard (375x440) the Themes list overlays the save bar too.

**Fix:** on open (touch), scroll the field into view with the save-bar offset; cap list height to the visual viewport minus the field bottom and save-bar height, and flip above the field when it won't fit; or lower the list's z-index beneath the save bar and let it scroll.

Screenshot: https://github.com/andrewgari/commander-lab/blob/wt/t_d54c718e/docs/design/genre/review/d06-phone-dropdown-vs-keyboard-savebar.png (design review figures on branch wt/t_d54c718e). Design review D6.
title: Deck Genre: phone autocomplete list opens off-screen and under the sticky save bar

body:
Found in design review of PR #145, head e495450. Severity: Medium (touch usability; on a phone the star is the only way to change the primary).

**Repro:** Open the Deck Genre section at 768px and 375px in touch emulation and measure the × and ☆ controls.
**Expected:** At least 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8 AA), ideally 44px on touch.
**Actual:** 11x12 px at 768 (touch), because the enlargement is keyed to `@media (max-width: 640px)`. 24x24 px on phone, below the 44px recommendation.

**Fix:** key the enlargement to `@media (pointer: coarse)` with ~2.75rem hit areas via padding or `::after`, keeping the chip height. On fine pointers, keep targets at least 24x24.

Screenshots: https://github.com/andrewgari/commander-lab/blob/wt/t_d54c718e/docs/design/genre/review/d05-touch-targets-768.png, https://github.com/andrewgari/commander-lab/blob/wt/t_d54c718e/docs/design/genre/review/d05-touch-targets-375.png (design review figures on branch wt/t_d54c718e). Design review D5.
title: Deck Genre: remove and star hit targets too small on tablet and phone touch

**Repro:** Journal > Archetype, type `noir` or `spel`.

body:
Found by the Update/Push E2E pass (t_ae23ea40) against origin/main 1dd9b38.

**Bug:** A deck whose only external link is Commander Salt (e.g. \`links: {commandersalt: {identifier: "99"}}\`) shows the Update/Push panel as:

> No external deck linked.
> [LINK EXTERNAL DECK]

That is wrong: the deck is linked. The panel only lists archidekt/moxfield providers (\`SyncControls.viewModel\` filters on \`p.provider === "archidekt" || "moxfield"\`), so a link-only provider is treated the same as no link. The "Link External Deck" button then invites the user to add a link that already exists.

**Repro:**
1. Seed or import a deck with only a Commander Salt link.
2. Open its deck page (\`/deck/<name>\`).
3. Look at the sync panel (\`#syncControls\`).

**Expected:** No Update/Push buttons, since Commander Salt cannot be updated or pushed. The text should say the deck is linked to Commander Salt and cannot be synced, not that no deck is linked. The Link button should only show when no link exists at all.

**Observed:** The text "No external deck linked." plus the Link button.

**Where:** \`static/js/sync_controls.js\` (\`viewModel\` / \`panelHtml\`, the \`state === "none"\` branch).

**Severity:** Low. No data is changed and no sync fires. It is misleading UI on a read-only provider.

Verified in the live E2E harness: \`GET /api/decks/commandersalt:99/sync/status\` returns the link, but the panel renders the empty state.
title: Deck sync panel says 'No external deck linked' for a Commander Salt-linked deck

body:
**Related PR:** https://github.com/andrewgari/commander-lab/pull/129

### Summary
During legacy preference verification of the Tune filter modes (PR #129, commit `9106b2b`), mode selection was found not to persist across page reload.

The Tune page template (`templates/deck_tune.html`) includes restoration logic `restore()` that reads `?mode=` from the URL on load. However, when a user switches modes by clicking radio buttons or toggling checkboxes, the page does not update the browser URL (via `history.replaceState` / `history.pushState`) and does not write to `localStorage`.

As a result:
1. Reloading the page drops the user back to the default flex mode (`Owned, plus in-deck and/or buy`).
2. Copying or bookmarking the URL after changing modes fails to preserve the active filter view.

### Reproduction Steps
1. Navigate to `/deck/Holy%20Hellfire/tune` in the browser.
2. Click **"Owned, not in a deck"** (Mode 1 / `free`).
3. Observe that the browser address bar still shows `/deck/Holy%20Hellfire/tune` without any `?mode=free` query parameter, and no local storage or cookie is set.
4. Refresh / reload the page in the browser.

### Expected Behavior
- Mode selection should survive page reload (e.g. by updating `window.location.search` / URL parameters via `history.replaceState` or storing preference in browser storage).
- The URL query string should reflect the selected mode and toggle state so links can be shared or reloaded.

### Actual Behavior
- Reloading the page resets the selection to `Owned, plus in-deck and/or buy` (flex default).
- The URL never updates when clicking mode buttons.

### Artifacts & Screenshots
- Screenshot: `after_change_then_reload.png` (captured in task `t_6ae91e5e` deliverable)
- Also verified: seeding `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` with keys like `mode` or `tune_mode` has no effect because nothing writes to or reads from storage.
title: Tune page: filter mode selection is not persisted across reload or reflected in URL

**Related PR:** https://github.com/andrewgari/commander-lab/pull/129

### Summary
During Playwright dogfooding of the new Tune filter modes (PR #129, commit `9106b2b`), Mode 3 was found to display in-deck wording on the page.

The feature specification states:
> 3. "Best card": best options regardless of ownership, with NO labeling or mention of pulling or stealing from other physical decks.

While the individual recommendation cards and swap lines do not mention donor decks or steal rules in Mode 3, the segmented radio button in the top filter bar retains the visible text label `"Owned, plus in-deck and/or buy"`. The string `"in-deck"` remains visible on screen while Best card is active.

### Reproduction Steps
1. Seed test inventory (Holy Hellfire deck with loose owned, in-deck owned, and unowned cards, e.g. `tests/e2e/tune_modes_fixture.py`).
2. Open `/deck/Holy%20Hellfire/tune` in the browser.
3. Click the **Best card** segmented radio button (`#src-best`).
4. Inspect the filter bar.

### Expected Behavior
No in-deck, pull, steal, or source-deck wording appears anywhere on the page when Mode 3 is active, including in the filter bar switcher (e.g. label phrased neutrally or contextual mode labels).

### Actual Behavior
The radio label `Owned, plus in-deck and/or buy` remains visible on the page while "Best card" is selected.

### Artifacts & Screenshots
- Screenshot: `tests/e2e/tune_modes_shots/mode3.png` (from dogfood task `t_43f883f0`)
- Test spec: `tests/e2e/test_tune_filter_modes_e2e.py`

body:
**Found by:** e2e verification of the Decommission feature (PRs #130/#132).

**Summary:** `registry.set_status` only auto-binds when a deck becomes `physical`. When a physical deck is moved to `retired` (or `digital`/`testing`) through `POST /api/decks/{id}/status`, its instances stay `in_deck` and point at the now non-physical deck. `POST /api/decks/{id}/decommission` then returns 400 ("only physical decks can be decommissioned"), so the cards cannot be returned to the owned pool through the feature.

**Repro (TestClient or curl, on a fresh Redis):**
1. Seed a digital deck with a Sol Ring in its cardlist, `POST /api/decks/archidekt:9103/status {"status":"physical"}` -> one Sol Ring instance is `in_deck`, deck_id 9103.
2. `POST /api/decks/archidekt:9103/status {"status":"retired"}` -> success.
3. `GET /api/instances` -> Sol Ring still `in_deck`, deck_id 9103.
4. `POST /api/decks/archidekt:9103/decommission` -> 400 `only physical decks can be decommissioned (deck status is 'retired')`.

**Expected:** leaving `physical` releases its in_deck instances to in_collection (same as decommission does), or decommission accepts retired decks that still hold bound cards.

**Test:** `tests/e2e/test_decommission_e2e.py::test_bug_status_dropdown_retire_releases_cards` (marked xfail strict; remove the marker when fixed).

Branch: wt/t_bf739761
title: Decommission: physical deck retired via status dropdown leaves cards bound in_deck; decommission then rejects it

body:
**Severity: low (naming / contract).**

Spec §2.6 names the flags `edhrec_card_missing`, `edhrec_commander_missing` and `rank_missing`. The implementation emits `edhrec_data_missing` for both the card-not-listed and commander-no-page cases, and does not emit `rank_missing`.

The UI and the warnings do not depend on the exact name, so this is only a contract mismatch. It matters if anything downstream filters on the flag names.

Decide whether to align the code with the spec or the spec with the code, and update whichever is wrong.

See docs/CARD_REVIEW_E2E_REPORT.md.
title: Card Review: missing-data flag names differ from spec §2.6 (low)

body:
**Severity: medium (quality question for domain review).**

Dogfood on Holy Hellfire (Kaalia of the Vast, digital): Temple of Triumph and Rugged Prairie are ruled Remove (strength 31-33). Their 5-card slates are mixed: Arena of Glory, Exotic Orchard, Bloodstained Mire (like-for-like lands), then Kaalia, Zenith Seeker and Rakdos, Patron of Chaos (non-lands).

Cutting a three-colour dual and replacing it with a creature or a spell breaks the mana base. It is not a swap. The replacement brief for a land should probably be like-for-like only, or the land should not be a Remove candidate at all without a mana-base check.

Needs a domain decision: should lands ever be Remove, and if so, should their slates be lands only?

See docs/CARD_REVIEW_E2E_REPORT.md.
title: Card Review: Remove verdicts on lands get spell replacements (mixed mode)

body:
**Severity: medium. Needs a product call (spec says 3-5).**

The replacement candidate pool is built only from the commander's EDHREC page (`analytics/card_eval/service.py` `_build_pool`). When EDHREC is unavailable, or the commander has no page, the pool is empty. The verdict still renders, with the right warning, but a Remove returns `replacements: []`. The UI shows "No better options found".

Reproduced in the E2E suite (`test_edhrec_unavailable_shows_verdict_and_empty_replacements`, and the no-page commander case) and in the dogfood run.

Spec §1 requires 3-5 replacements on Remove. §4.4 says a short pool returns what passes with `pool_exhausted: true`, but that pool is still EDHREC-only.

Questions for Andrew:
1. Should the pool fall back to Scryfall or the local card DB (filtered by role and identity) when EDHREC has no page?
2. Or is an empty slate with an explicit reason the intended behaviour, with the UI message improved to say "EDHREC is unavailable, so no suggestions"?

Current UI copy does not name the cause.
title: Card Review: Remove verdict with EDHREC down or no commander page returns zero replacements

body:
**Severity: high (verdict quality).**

With EDHREC data missing for a card and no model-sourced role (HF disabled or unclassified), every strength component is `None`. `compute_strength` returns 0.0, and the card is ruled Remove with confidence 0.60 and a 5-card replacement slate.

Live repro (dogfood, real Archidekt deck 417707, digital, commander Kaalia of the Vast): Baneslayer Angel, Hellkite Charger, Basandra, Battle Seraph, Homeward Path all come back `strength 0.0, band cut_candidate, p_keep_prior 0.0`. The physical deck 5620189 has An Unearthly Child, Barren Glory, Absolute Virtue at 0.0. Baneslayer Angel is a staple in any deck that can run it.

Cause: `analytics/card_eval/service.py` sets `role_conf` only from roles with `source == "model"`, so heuristic and EDHREC-tag roles are ignored. With EDHREC and the model both empty, all components are None and the weighted mean falls back to 0.

Spec: docs/single-card-review-spec.md §2.6 says a missing EDHREC entry drops I and S and keeps the role term (E = R). A missing rank uses R = 50. Neither gives 0.

Expected: an unknown or neutral score (for example 50) with a flag, not a Remove at 0. Probably also should not be a cut candidate at all.

See docs/CARD_REVIEW_E2E_REPORT.md (dogfood section).
title: Card Review: cards with no EDHREC entry and no model role score 0.0 and are ruled Remove
